chapter: Return to Atlanta and move north
title: His mother's death and signing the contract
summary: Green confirms his lifetime contract with Achet, says his mother died in 1927 when he was nine, and he agrees to go north with George Robey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you really have a lifetime contract with her?
So she knew you were back in town, and she told you, now's the time to go to New York?
Yeah. Yeah, because, see, my mother passed. See, my mother died, see.
You were only about nine or ten at this point?

Nine, I was nine years old, yeah. And, yeah, I think that was, yeah, it was 1927. I beg your pardon. That's when it was. And so, you know, I was in Atlanta for a few months or so, you know, but I wasn't the same person. I got kind of different after mother left, you see.

So Miss Lucille Achet, she figured it would be nice for me to go away like, you know, wouldn't be around Atlanta, Georgia, be thinking about my mother or something, you know. So I was a happy child, you see, very playful, you see, and so that's what happened. We signed the contracts and all, and then we went with Mr. George Robey, you know. He bought a car.
